# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1065

## Korean source

```text
  1|1065화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|
  6|전투에서의 패배는 곧 끝장을 의미한다.
  7|
  8|수만 명이 정면으로 맞붙어 싸우는 대규모 회전(會戰)의 경우에는 특히나 그렇다.
  9|
 10|가까스로 살아남은 패자들의 앞에 놓인 운명은 단 두 가지다.
 11|
 12|포로가 되거나, 세상 끝까지 도망치거나.
 13|
 14|이는 선택할 수도, 거부할 수도 없다.
 15|
 16|하지만 승자는 다르다.
 17|
 18|그렇기에 지금으로부터 사흘 전, 대설산(大雪山)을 둘러싼 혈전이 아군의 대승으로 막을 내린 직후 우리에게는 새로운 선택지가 주어졌다.
 19|
 20|전투의 여파를 수습한 뒤 계속해서 감숙성을 지킬 것인가.
 21|
 22|아니면 또 다른 어딘가에서 밀려들고 있을 암천의 군세를 막기 위해 이동할 것인가.
 23|
 24|그리고 우리의 선택은 후자(後者)였다.
 25|
 26|아니, 내 의사를 모두가 존중해 주었다는 것이 더 정확한 표현이었다.
 27|
 28|‘저는 이만 떠나겠습니다. 해야 할 일이 있어요.’
 29|
 30|설원(雪原)이 불길과 연기로 뒤덮인 날이었다.
 31|
 32|수만여 구의 시신을 집어삼킨 화염은 영원히 꺼지지 않을 것처럼 타오르는 중이었고, 내가 불현듯 던진 한마디는 그 광경을 지켜보며 하염없이 눈물을 흘리던 이들에게 너무나도 가혹하게 느껴졌을 것이다.
 33|
 34|하지만 온전히 슬픔에 잠길 시간조차 빼앗겼음에도, 그들은 나를 비난하지 않았다.
 35|
 36|단 한 사람도.
 37|
 38|다만 공동파의 장문인인 현천진인만이 앞으로 나서 짧은 물음을 던졌을 뿐이었다.
 39|
 40|‘어디로 갈 생각인가?’
 41|
 42|내 대답은 처음부터 정해져 있었다.
 43|
 44|시스템은 이미 퀘스트라는 나침반으로 다음 행선지를 명확하게 가리키고 있었으니까.
 45|
 46|‘청해(靑海). 청해입니다.’
 47|
 48|‘그렇다는 건.’
 49|
 50|‘예. 놈들이 오고 있습니다.’
 51|
 52|이해할 수 없을 정도의 확신이 담긴 내 음성에도, 현천진인은 이유를 묻지 않았다.
 53|
 54|다만 무거운 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였을 뿐이었다.
 55|
 56|‘다시 한번 세상이 피로 물들겠군.’
 57|
 58|‘그럴 겁니다. 분명히.’
 59|
 60|‘그곳에서도 놈들을 상대로 대승을 거둔다면, 이 저주받은 전쟁을 종식시킬 수 있으리라 생각하나?’
 61|
 62|‘한 걸음 더 가까워질 겁니다. 그리고 이번에 내디딜 걸음은, 그 어느 때보다 크고 깊겠죠.’
 63|
 64|‘천주(天主)에게 닿을 만큼?’
 65|
 66|‘그러리라 믿습니다.’
 67|
 68|‘그렇다면 우리 공동파 또한 자네와 함께하겠네.’
 69|
 70|‘……!’
 71|
 72|‘끝에 다다르기 전까지는 결코 멈추지 않겠네. 지금쯤 저 구름 위에서 원시천존(號出天等)의 보살핌을 받고 있을 넋들을 위해서라도.’
 73|
 74|만약 현천진인이 살아남은 암천의 교도들을 도살할 때와 같은 살기를 흘리고 있었다면, 나는 그의 합류를 거절했을 것이다.
 75|
 76|하지만 이미 많은 것을 잃어버린 노도사(老道士)의 눈동자는 더없이 맑았으며, 이는 한바탕 분노와 슬픔을 쏟아낸 공동파의 제자들 또한 마찬가지였다.
 77|
 78|‘좋습니다.’
 79|
 80|그렇게 현천진인을 비롯한 일백여 명의 공동파 제자들이 합류하게 되었지만, 이는 단지 시작에 불과했다.
 81|
 82|‘무림말학 혁소평. 감히 이 자리를 빌어 사문의 죄를 청하고자 합니다.’
 83|
 84|종남일룡(終南一龍) 혁소평.
 85|
 86|더불어 혈전 속에서 가까스로 목숨을 부지한 삼백여 명의 종남파 제자들은 병장기를 내려놓고 무릎을 꿇었다.
 87|
 88|노호검객 송일과 태을무정검 황보엄.
 89|
 90|이제는 죽고 없는 사문의 두 어른이 지은 죄를 알게 된 그들의 낯빛은 부끄러움과 슬픔으로 가득했고, 온 힘을 다해 악문 잇새 사이로는 핏줄기가 흘렀다.
 91|
 92|만일 종남파의 장문인인 풍운검군(風雲劍君)이 극심한 부상으로 의식불명의 상태에 빠지지만 않았더라면, 그 또한 제자들과 함께 무릎을 꿇고 죄를 청했을 것이다.
 93|
 94|그리고 그런 종남파의 제자들을 한참이나 말없이 응시하던 현천진인은 이렇게 말했다.
 95|
 96|‘아비의 죄가 자식의 것이 아니듯, 스승의 죄 역시 제자의 몫이 아닌 법. 한데 종남의 제자들은 어찌하여 빈도에게 죗값을 청하는가.’
 97|
 98|‘……!’
 99|
100|‘그럼에도 죗값을 달게 받고자 한다면, 좋다. 여기 있는 진 도우(道友)를 따라 올곧고 밝은 방향으로 나아가거라. 그것이 종남파의 새로운 길이 될 것이니.’
101|
102|현명하고 자애로운 노도사의 말에, 혁소평과 종남파의 제자들은 크게 절을 올린 뒤 내게 지극한 예를 갖추어 포권지례를 취했다.
103|
104|‘한 치의 어긋남도 없는 정도(正道)를 걷고자 하는바, 진 대협께 합류를 청합니다.’
105|
106|용봉표국의 사건 이후 처음으로 맞대면하게 된 혁소평이었다.
107|
108|종남파 제일의 후기지수로서 십봉룡(十鳳龍)의 한 자리를 차지하고 있던 녀석과 나 사이에 놓인 간극은 그때보다도 아득하게 벌어져 있었다.
109|
110|따라서 종남파와 여러 날을 함께 하며 감숙에서 시간을 보내는 와중에도 멀리서만 스쳐 지나갈 수밖에 없었다.
111|
112|아마도 그래서였을 것이다.
113|
114|혁소평의 기세와 눈빛이, 마지막에 보았던 것과는 비교도 할 수 없을 만큼 진중하고 깊어졌다는 사실을 그제야 깨달은 것은.
115|
116|‘그 제안, 기꺼이 받아들이겠습니다.’
117|
118|나는 모처럼 예의를 갖추어 종남파의 합류를 승낙했고, 두 문파의 합류로 순식간에 오백여 명까지 불어난 상황을 지켜보던 한 사람이 다가왔다.
119|
120|‘이 정도로도 부족할 텐데. 안 그런가?’
121|
122|‘글쎄. 어중이떠중이들로 머릿수를 채우는 것보단 훨씬 낫겠지.’
123|
124|‘어째서인지 귀가 간지러운데. 기분 탓이겠지?’
125|
126|‘아닐 수도 있고.’
127|
128|짐짓 딴청을 피우는 내 모습에 실소를 흘린 흑룡마문(黑龍魔門)의 신임 문주는, 오와 열을 맞춰 도열한 자신의 새로운 수하들을 가리켰다.
129|
130|‘오백. 시간이 촉박했지만 자원한 이들 중에서도 철저하게 가려 뽑았네. 비록 구파일방의 제자들에게는 미치지 못하더라도 충성심과 투지만큼은 보장하지.’
131|
132|‘그래서, 내게 맡기겠다?’
133|
134|‘아니. 데려가도록 허락해 주면 고맙겠군.’
135|
136|‘뭐?’
137|
138|‘흑룡마문주 사마표 이하 오백 인. 화룡각주(火龍閣主)께 합류를 청합니다. 부디 지난날의 과오를 조금이나마 씻고 천하를 위해 싸우도록 허락해 주십시오.’
139|
140|‘……!’
141|
142|순간, 나는 잠시 말문이 막혔다.
143|
144|만약 그때 자그마한 노인을 목에 대롱대롱 매단 거한이 이렇게 외치지 않았다면, 울컥하는 마음을 쉽게 억누르지 못했을 정도로.
145|
146|‘태산이! 태산이도 간다! 각주랑 끝까지 간다!’
147|
148|‘이런 염병할! 살살 좀 뛰라고! 제발!’
149|
150|모두가 약속이라도 한 것처럼 동시에 웃음을 터트렸다.
151|
152|나와 사마표, 화룡각 대원들과 구파일방의 생존자들.
153|
154|그리고 기쁠 때나 슬플 때나 늘 무미건조한 표정을 짓고 있던 금의위 천호 정호군까지도.
155|
156|‘제법 재미있는 족속들이군. 그대와 같은 무림인들은.’
157|
158|‘그래? 기왕 말 나온 김에 더 재미있는 얘기 해 줄까?’
159|
160|‘더 재미있는 얘기?’
161|
162|‘응. 하늘 같은 열후한테 반말 찍찍해 대다가 강제 전역당할 위기에 처한 어느 금의위 천호에 대한 이야긴데. 놀랍게도 얘랑 너랑 성씨가 같네. 신기한 우연이지?’
163|
164|‘……이렇게 나올 건가?’
165|
166|‘그러니까 잘해 봐. 이렇게 나오지 않도록.’
167|
168|정호군은 못 당하겠다는 듯이 고개를 절레절레 내저었고, 이내 철탑 같은 자세로 내게 군례(軍禮)를 취했다.
169|
170|‘그렇다면 부디 명령을.’
171|
172|‘청해. 청해성으로 간다. 전속력을 다해서.’
173|
174|‘신, 금의위 천호 정호군. 지엄하신 상산후의 명을 받듭니다.’
175|
176|그리하여 지금으로부터 이틀 전.
177|
178|마지막 한 조각이었던 금의위까지 합류하며 이천여 명에 가까워진 병력은, 짧은 휴식을 뒤로한 채 곧장 청해성으로 향했다.
179|
180|물론 그 과정에서 몇몇 이들은 암천이 다시 한번 감숙성을 노릴지도 모른다는 신중론을 제기하기도 했지만, 궁성은 짤막한 한 마디로 모든 우려를 종식시켰다.
181|
182|‘북부가 움직이고 있다.’
183|
184|당연하게도 이는 단순히 감숙성 북부를 말하는 것이 아니었다.
185|
186|장성으로 구분된 천하 전체에서의 북부. 아울러 그 드넓은 땅을 지배하는 두 패자(霸者)를 뜻함이었다.
187|
188|하북의 맹호, 하북팽가.
189|
190|더불어 푸르른 초원의 하늘마저 손에 넣게 된 산서성의 창룡(蒼龍), 태원진가.
191|
192|‘화살마다 쏘아지는 속도는 다를지라도, 방향만 흔들리지 않으면 결국은 표적에 닿는 법이지.’
193|
194|예컨대 궁성과 금의위는 먼저 쏘아진 화살이었다.
195|
196|실로 궁성다운 비유였고, 그 후로는 누구도 감히 반박하지 못했다.
197|
198|비단 그 말을 한 이가 궁성이기 때문만은 아니었다.
199|
200|북부의 창룡과 맹호가 날개를 펴고, 발톱을 드러낸 이상 감숙성의 안전은 어느 정도 보장된 것이라는 사실을 모두가 알고 있었으니까.
201|
202|그리고 감숙성을 떠나기 직전 벌어진 짧은 숙청(肅淸)의 시간은, 혹시 모를 후환을 송두리째 제거하기에 충분했다.
203|
204|‘마지막으로 남길 말이 있나? 변명은 됐고, 유언이라면 들어주지.’
205|
206|‘나, 나는 암천과 결탁하지 않았소. 뭔가 오해가 있었던 것이 분명하오!’
207|
208|‘소문주, 아니 문주! 도대체 왜 이러는 거요. 작고하신 선친(先親)과 내가 의형제나 다름없는 각별한 사이라는 걸 알지 않소!’
209|
210|‘그래, 알지. 배신도 함께할 정도였으니까. 어찌나 각별한 사이였는지 아버지께서 전부 세세하게 기록도 해 두셨던데…… 알고 있었나?’
211|
212|‘……!’
213|
214|감숙 무림의 미래를 결정짓는 중차대한 회의에서, 배신자들을 추궁하는 재판장으로 변해 버린 공간이 삽시간에 얼어붙었다.
215|
216|부릅뜬 눈. 파르르 떨리는 입꼬리.
217|
218|그런 그들의 모습에 작게 한숨을 내쉰 사마표가 품에서 낡은 서책 한 권을 꺼내 탁자에 올려 두었다.
219|
220|‘역시 몰랐던 모양이군. 의심 정도는 해 볼 법도 했을 텐데.’
221|
222|그 철두철미한 흑야왕 사마공이 이토록 확실한 증거를 남겼다는 것에 대해 나조차도 뜻밖이라고 생각했으니, 수십여 년간 생전의 그를 알아 왔던 저들이야 오죽했을까.
223|
224|하지만 사마표는 아랑곳하지 않고 말을 이어 갔다.
225|
226|아버지에 대한 일말의 씁쓸함이 담긴 음성과 벌레들을 바라보는 듯한 눈빛으로.
227|
228|‘그래서, 유언은?’
229|
230|그것이 결정타였다.
231|
232|‘이, 이런 대가리에 피도 안 마른 애새끼 따위가! 이놈! 의숙부나 다름없는 나를 죽일 셈이냐!’
233|
234|‘허. 허허. 결국, 결국 이리 되었는가.’
235|
236|궁지에 몰린 쥐새끼가 선택할 수 있는 길은 두 가지뿐이었다.
237|
238|그 앙증맞은 앞니라도 무기 삼아 달려들거나. 혹은 모든 것을 체념하고 운명을 받아들이거나.
239|
240|그리고 어리석게도 전자를 택한 이들을 기다리고 있던 것은.
241|
242|‘이야기 끝났다. 태산아.’
243|

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Even after spending several days alongside the Zhongnan Sect in Gansu, I’d only ever passed him at a distance. Maybe that was why I’d only just noticed how much more serious his bearing had become, how much deeper his gaze.

[P51]
“I’d be glad to have you.”

[P52]
For once, I accepted an offer with proper courtesy. Our numbers had swelled to around five hundred with the two sects joining us, and someone watching it all came over.

[P53]
“Even this won’t be enough. Don’t you think?”

[P54]
“Maybe. Still better than padding our numbers with any old riffraff.”

[P55]
“Funny. My ears are itching. Must be my imagination.”

[P56]
“Maybe not.”

[P57]
The new Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate gave a dry laugh at my feigned innocence, then pointed to his new followers, lined up in orderly ranks.

[P58]
“Five hundred. Time was short, but I chose them carefully from the volunteers. They may not measure up to the Disciples of the Nine Sects and One Gang, but I can vouch for their loyalty and fighting spirit.”

[P59]
“So you’re putting them under my command?”

[P60]
“No. I’d be grateful if you let them come with you.”

[P61]
“What?”

[P62]
“I, Sama Pyo, Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, and five hundred men ask to join the Fire Dragon Pavilion Master. Please allow us to fight for the realm and make up, however little, for our past wrongs.”

[P63]
“…!”

[P64]
For a moment, I couldn’t speak.

[P65]
I might not have been able to hold back the emotion welling up inside me if a giant with a little old man dangling from his neck hadn’t shouted right then.

[P66]
“Taishan’s going! Taishan’s going too! Taishan will go with the Pavilion Master to the end!”

[P67]
“Goddamn it! Stop bouncing around so much! Please!”

[P68]
Everyone burst out laughing at once, as if they’d planned it.

[P69]
Me, Sama Pyo, the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, and the survivors of the Nine Sects and One Gang.

[P70]
Even Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, whose expression never changed whether he was happy or sad.

[P71]
“You martial artists are quite an amusing lot.”

[P72]
“Really? Since you brought it up, want to hear something even funnier?”

[P73]
“Something funnier?”

[P74]
“Yeah. It’s about a certain Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard who keeps speaking casually to a lofty marquis and is now in danger of being forced out of the service. Amazingly, he has the same surname as you. What a coincidence, huh?”

[P75]
“…Is that how you’re going to play this?”

[P76]
“Then watch yourself, so I don’t have to.”

[P77]
Jeong Hogun shook his head as though there was no winning with me. Then he stood as straight as an iron tower and saluted.

[P78]
“Then please give your orders.”

[P79]
“Qinghai. We’re going to Qinghai Province. At full speed.”

[P80]
“I, Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, accept the solemn command of the Marquis of Shangshan.”

[P81]
And so, two days ago, the Embroidered Uniform Guard joined us as the final piece of our force. Now nearly two thousand strong, we took a brief rest and headed straight for Qinghai Province.

[P82]
A few people raised the cautious possibility that Dark Heaven might target Gansu again. The Bow Saint put those concerns to rest with a single remark.

[P83]
“The North is moving.”

[P84]
Naturally, he didn’t mean northern Gansu.

[P85]
He meant the North of the realm beyond the Great Wall, and the two powers that ruled those vast lands.

[P86]
The fierce tiger of Hebei: the Hebei Peng Family.

[P87]
And the Azure Dragon of Shanxi Province: the Jin Family of Taiyuan, who had now claimed even the skies above the green grasslands.

[P88]
“Arrows may fly at different speeds, but so long as they hold their course, each will eventually strike its target.”

[P89]
The Bow Saint and the Embroidered Uniform Guard, for example, were arrows shot ahead of the rest.

[P90]
It was a metaphor worthy of the Bow Saint. No one argued after that.

[P91]
Not merely because he was the Bow Saint. Everyone knew that with the Azure Dragon and the fierce tiger of the North spreading their wings and baring their claws, Gansu was reasonably safe.

[P92]
And the brief purge just before we left Gansu was enough to remove any threat that might remain.

[P93]
“Anything you want to say before you die? Spare me the excuses. I’ll hear your last words.”

[P94]
“I—I never colluded with Dark Heaven. There must be some misunderstanding!”

[P95]
“Young Sect Leader—no, Sect Leader! Why are you doing this? You know your late father and I were practically sworn brothers!”

[P96]
“I know. Close enough to betray us together. You were so close that my father wrote it all down in detail… Did you know that?”

[P97]
“…!”

[P98]
The meeting meant to decide the future of Gansu’s Murim had become a trial of its traitors. The room froze.

[P99]
Eyes wide. Mouths trembling.

[P100]
Sama Pyo gave a quiet sigh at the sight of them, took a battered old book from inside his robe, and set it on the table.

[P101]
“So you didn’t know. I’d have thought you might at least suspect.”

[P102]
Even I was surprised that the meticulous Black Night King, Sima Gong, had left such conclusive evidence behind. How much more shocked must those men have been, after knowing him for decades?

[P103]
Sama Pyo went on. There was a trace of bitterness toward his father in his voice, and he looked at the men as though they were insects.

[P104]
“So. Any last words?”

[P105]
That did it.

[P106]
“You—you little brat still wet behind the ears! You dare kill me, your uncle in all but name?!”

[P107]
“Heh. Heh heh. So this is how it ends.”

[P108]
A cornered rat had only two choices.

[P109]
Charge with its adorable little front teeth as its only weapon, or give up and accept its fate.

[P110]
And waiting for the fools who chose to charge was—

[P111]
“Conversation’s over, Taishan.”

[P112]
“Yaaawn. Taishan nearly fell asleep listening.”

[P113]
Tiger Giant Child Taishan: designated hitter for the Gansu Black Dragons, with a career batting average of .999.

[P114]
*Wham! Whaaam!*

[P115]
I was there in case anything went wrong, but I never had to step in.

[P116]
Taishan’s two-section staff was gleefully spitting fire—no, blood.

[P117]
The Black Dragon Demon Gate elder who had called Sama Pyo a wet-behind-the-ears brat and charged at him no longer had a head to hold any blood. Several Sect Leaders and Family Heads fled with all their might, only to be surrounded as soon as they left the pavilion.

[P118]
By Black Dragon Demon Gate warriors who had sworn loyalty to their new lord.

[P119]
And by their own followers and Disciples.

[P120]
“G-Gangpyeong! How could you do this to me?!”

[P121]
“How could *you* do what you did, Sect Leader?”

[P122]
“Guard the way! Hurry! No—this is an order from your Sect Leader! Stop those men right—”

[P123]
“Shut your filthy mouth.”

[P124]
“What?”

[P125]
“Because of you, my Master, my Junior Sister, and my Martial Nephew died! You deceived your master and betrayed your ancestors. Disciples of the Gorang Sword Sect, execute the Sect Leader here and now, as our sect rules demand!”

[P126]
“What are the members of the Lanzhou Hyuk Family doing?!”

[P127]
“Please don’t hold it against us, Family Head. You betrayed us first.”

[P128]
“Y-you dare…!”

[P129]
*Slice! Thud-thud-thud!*

[P130]
Spears and blades came at them from every direction. Around a dozen Sect Leaders and Family Heads died with their eyes wide open, unable even to leave proper last words.

[P131]
A miserable end for men who had led Gansu’s Murim, each the head of a faction with a substantial following.

[P132]
The young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate didn’t so much as blink as twenty renowned masters in all were killed or captured.

[P133]
He watched it all with calm, cold eyes. Then, touching his teacup, which had long since gone cold, he spoke out of the blue.

[P134]
“Should I have them bring fresh tea?”

[P135]
“No. It tastes awful, and we don’t have time. Besides, that scatterbrained man will be joining us soon. Tea will just turn my stomach.”

[P136]
“Great Sir—does he really know the fastest route to Qinghai Province?”

[P137]
“Ma Junggeol told me he does, anyway. I don’t know what he did when he was young, but apparently he knows the terrain inside out.”

[P138]
“I see. Then our business here is done. I’ll go with you, Pavilion Master.”

[P139]
Sama Pyo nodded and stood.

[P140]
Only fifteen minutes ago, more than twenty faces had crowded around the table. Now no one remained at it, and all that lay on top were overturned teacups and a battered old book.

[P141]
“Aren’t you taking it?”

[P142]
“I don’t need it anymore.”

[P143]
With that, Sama Pyo left. After a moment’s thought, I picked up the book.

[P144]
It had served its purpose and been cast aside, but it was still something his dead father had left behind.

[P145]
I clicked my tongue, turned the first page without thinking, and understood what Sama Pyo had really meant.

[P146]
“…Huh.”

[P147]
I let out a dry laugh and set the book down.

[P148]
No. Not a book.

[P149]
Just a bundle of yellowed pages without a single character written on them. It had plainly spent years gathering dust somewhere, never once put to use.

[P150]
“Blood really does tell. In a good way.”

[P151]
I muttered the words and walked on through the smell of blood from the traitors’ bodies.

[P152]
Two days passed after that. Then another three went by as we made our way over mountain slopes so rough they made me want to curse.

[P153]
“Hey, young man. What’s your name?”

[P154]
“Jin Taekyung. You know that’s the twenty-fourth time I’ve told you, right?”

[P155]
“Ah, yes. Jang Sam.”

[P156]
“How the hell does Jin Taekyung become Jang Sam… Forget it. What do you want?”

[P157]
“Well, it’s nothing terribly important.”

[P158]
“Tell me anyway. While I’m still speaking politely to you.”

[P159]
“It’s just that I can’t for the life of me tell where we are.”

[P160]
“…What?”

[P161]
“I asked where we are.”

[P162]
“Fucking hell.”

[P163]
I was seized by the urge to kill that lunatic guide for spouting this insanity with a straight face.

[P164]
A fierce, overpowering urge, strong enough to snap my last thread of self-control.

[P165]
*Step.*

[P166]
I couldn’t hold back any longer. But just as I approached Great Sir to let our fists do the talking—

[P167]
*Ding!*

[P168]
> **System**
>
> Entered **Qinghai Province**.

[P169]
A clear chime rang in my ears, gluing my momentarily severed thread of self-control back together.

“…Huh.”

[P147]
I let out a dry laugh and set the book down.

[P148]
No. Not a book.

[P149]
Just a bundle of yellowed pages without a single character written on them. It had plainly spent years gathering dust somewhere, never once put to use.

[P150]
“Blood really does tell. In a good way.”

[P151]
I muttered the words and walked on through the smell of blood from the traitors’ bodies.

[P152]
Two days passed after that. Then another three went by as we made our way over mountain slopes so rough they made me want to curse.

[P153]
“Hey, young man. What’s your name?”

[P154]
“Jin Taekyung. You know that’s the twenty-fourth time I’ve told you, right?”

[P155]
“Ah, yes. Jang Sam.”

[P156]
“How the hell does Jin Taekyung become Jang Sam… Forget it. What do you want?”

[P157]
“Well, it’s nothing terribly important.”

[P158]
“Tell me anyway. While I’m still speaking politely to you.”

[P159]
“It’s just that I can’t for the life of me tell where we are.”

[P160]
“…What?”

[P161]
“I asked where we are.”

[P162]
“Fucking hell.”

[P163]
I was seized by the urge to kill that lunatic guide for spouting this insanity with a straight face.

[P164]
A fierce, overpowering urge, strong enough to snap my last thread of self-control.

[P165]
*Step.*

[P166]
I couldn’t hold back any longer. But just as I approached Great Sir to let our fists do the talking—

[P167]
*Ding!*

[P168]
> **System**
>
> Entered **Qinghai Province**.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
